record.context_brief: Dual and holographic descriptions of QCD
record.original_question: Can a weakly coupled dual or holographic theory for real QCD be constructed and proven, so that low- and intermediate-energy strong dynamics can be calculated from a dual theory rather than chosen through partly arbitrary five-dimensional effective models?

evidence.quote: Note that the theory dual to QCD has not been constructed up to now.
A disadvantage of the method is that the duality between QCD and the five-dimensional effective theory is not proven.
As a result, the choice of the latter is somewhat arbitrary.
One may hope that in the future, a lowenergy effective theory for QCD might be derived in the frameworks of this approach.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) is the SU(3) non-abelian gauge theory of quarks and gluons whose coupling becomes strong at low and intermediate energies, making perturbative computations of hadronic observables (masses, form factors, decay constants, condensates) intractable. Gauge/gravity-type dualities suggest that strongly coupled gauge theories may admit weakly coupled dual descriptions in terms of a higher-dimensional gravitational/string theory; in practice, "holographic QCD" is currently implemented through five-dimensional effective field theories (e.g. hard-wall and soft-wall AdS/QCD models) whose field content, background geometry, boundary conditions, and potentials are postulated by hand to reproduce known QCD features.

Problem. Construct an explicit weakly coupled dual (holographic) theory T whose strong-coupling partition function and correlators are rigorously equivalent to those of real four-dimensional QCD with the physical gauge group SU(3) and the observed quark content and masses, and prove the duality. Concretely:

(a) Specify a higher-dimensional (string- or gravity-)theory T, including its field content, background, and action, as a function of the QCD parameters (gauge coupling, quark masses, number of flavors N_f = 6, number of colors N_c = 3).

(b) Establish a precise dictionary between gauge-invariant operators of QCD and fields of T, and prove that correlation functions of QCD operators (in particular two- and three-point functions of currents and of hadronic interpolating operators) coincide with those computed from T at weak coupling.

(c) Using T, derive — rather than postulate — the five-dimensional effective description used in AdS/QCD, and compute low- and intermediate-energy hadronic quantities (meson and baryon spectra, decay constants, form factors, chiral condensate) from first principles within T.

Does such a weakly coupled dual theory T for real QCD exist, and can the duality be proven?
artifact.status_search_result: No exact weakly coupled holographic dual of real QCD with N_c = 3 has been constructed or proven. AdS/CFT is rigorously known only for highly supersymmetric/large-N gauge theories, and bottom-up AdS/QCD models remain phenomenological five-dimensional effective theories whose duality to QCD is unproven. Recent reviews on holographic QCD continue to describe this as an outstanding open problem.

status_evidence.title: Holographic QCD (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Bottom-up holographic models of QCD use five-dimensional effective theories whose precise relation to QCD is conjectural.
status_evidence.claim: A proven weakly coupled dual of real QCD has not been constructed; existing holographic QCD models are effective and phenomenological.

status_evidence.title: AdS/QCD and Holographic QCD reviews
status_evidence.snippet: The dual of QCD is unknown; bottom-up models with hard/soft walls are introduced as approximations.
status_evidence.claim: The exact holographic dual of QCD remains unknown.
